title: Nutritional Screening in Hospitalized Patients with Acute Pancreatitis: A Comparative Study in Mexico
content: Background: Acute pancreatitis (AP) is an acute inflammatory condition with high metabolic demands; however, early detection of nutritional risk is underestimated and there is no universal consensus on which is most effective for predicting nutritional risk. Objectives: To compare the effectiveness of different nutritional screening tools in identifying nutritional risk in patients with AP. Methods: A cross-sectional analytical study was conducted at Civil Hospital of Guadalajara "Fray Antonio Alcalde" between May 2023 and May 2025. Hospitalized patients diagnosed with mild to moderate AP were included. Nutritional screening tools and anthropometric, demographic, clinical, and biochemical variables were also recorded. Results: Nutritional risk was found in 55.3% patients with SGA, 43.2% in MST, and 38.6% in NRS-2002 and SNAQ and 10.6% in MUST scales. Overweight was present in 43.2% of patients and obesity in 24.2%. Significant BMI difference was observed between groups (p = 0.02). Moderate patients with AP had 4.07 times higher probability of nutritional risk compared to those with mild AP (p = 0.02). The NRS-2002 and SNAQ scales achieved the highest diagnostic performance with moderate agreement (κ = 0.55 and κ = 0.52). Conclusions: Nutritional risk is highly prevalent in patients with AP, showing a significant increase as clinical severity progresses. The NRS-2002 and SNAQ scales proved to be the most effective screening tools in concordance with SGA. While higher BMI may seem protective, it could act as a confounding factor for nutritional risk during the acute phases of the disease.
